content: 1. The solubility of atazanavir decreases as pH increases. When H2-receptor antagonists (H2RAs) are coadministered, plasma concentrations of atazanavir are significantly reduced. For treatment-naïve patients, atazanavir should be taken either simultaneously with the H2RA or at least 10 hours afterward. For treatment-experienced patients, refer to dosage adjustment recommendations. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, adjust the fedratinib dose as described above. 4. Atazanavir and cobicistat both increase the levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including transdermal and intranasal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed until stable effects are achieved. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including transdermal and transmucosal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed until stable effects are achieved. 7. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4. 8. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Atazanavir decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor fexinidazole for reduced efficacy due to decreased plasma concentrations of its active metabolites (M1 and M2). 11. Cobicistat and fidaxomicin increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 12. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of futibatinib with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of futibatinib toxicities. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 18. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce gilteritinib dosage in patients with serious or life-threatening toxicity. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 21. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. In clinical trials, coadministration of atazanavir with glecaprevir increased the risk of ALT elevations. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases ibrutinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. 24. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Substantially reduced plasma concentrations of atazanavir are expected if PPIs are coadministered. PPI doses should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 26. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, administer 500 mg lapatinib once daily and increase the dose to the indicated level once cobicistat is discontinued. 28. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases larotrectinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases lefamulin levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases lemborexant levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 31. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of lenacapavir by inhibiting P-gp, UGT1A1, and CYP3A metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Drugs that inhibit these pathways may significantly increase lenacapavir plasma concentrations. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases leniolisib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
